text:
My mother had a tooth extracted and said it was the most painful thing she'd ever experienced. It hurt from the injection. I understand it's difficult, but the problem is, the injection didn't numb her gums. In the end, she needed three injections. When the extraction was performed, she was told to raise her hand if it hurt. When she raised her hand, she pressed it down and told her not to. I was even more confused. My mother's cheek is still swollen and in severe pain. I feel so bad for bringing her here. Just one time is enough.

*** Update 22/11/68 reply:
Two days after the extraction, my mother was in so much pain that I called the clinic myself. They apologized because the extraction was difficult. That was it.

Not enough anesthetic? But why did the injection numb her cheekbone instead of her gums? So, another injection was needed (for the lower tooth extraction).
Later, it was discovered that the extraction site was infected with pus, so she had to go to another hospital for further treatment.
I've had difficult teeth extracted elsewhere, but never for such prolonged pain or treatment.
